name: Slovakia
summary: Only children are protected: minors keep their full intestate share, adults half. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Slovakia has no trusts, and foundations are for public benefit.
reserved_share: Descendants only: minors must receive at least their full intestate share, adults at least half (Civil Code, Act 40/1964, s. 479). Contrary parts of a will are void unless the descendant is disinherited. Spouse and parents are not protected.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Slovakia is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. Trusts and trust-like institutes are not part of Slovak law. Foundations (nadácie) are governed by Act 34/2002 for publicly beneficial purposes; a private foundation proposal exists but its status was not confirmed.
open_questions: Status of the proposed private foundation (Accace 2023 note) was not confirmed.
Whether Slovak law now recognises a trust-like institute is contradicted by sources (a 2024 abstract says no).

sources.title: HCCH status table: Convention of 1 July 1985 on the Law Applicable to Trusts and on their Recognition
sources.publisher: Hague Conference on Private International Law
